newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-NSW WIN DESPITE LATE SOUTH AUSTRALIA FLOURISH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NSW WIN DESPITE LATE SOUTH AUSTRALIA FLOURISH.

text.p: An extraordinary late-order batting flourish on Monday was not enough to save defending Sheffield Shield champions South Australia from a crushing defeat by New South Wales.
New South Wales thrashed South Australia by 143 runs despite a record 10th wicket partnership of 87 between off-spinner Brad Young and Mark Harrity.
Chasing 452 for victory, South Australia were dismissed for 308 after resuming on the final day on 174 for six.
Middle-order batsman Darren Lehmann took his overnight score from 62 to 97 before he misjudged a pull shot against pace bowler Phil Alley and dragged the ball on to his wicket.
Young had resumed on five and played a subdued role in partnership with Lehmann before producing a superb flourish of runs.
Young almost singlehandedly broke a 67-year-old record for the 10th wicket in matches between the two states. Harrity contributed just two runs to the partnership of 87.
South Australia slumped to 221 for nine soon after Lehmann's dismissal. Young then began to savage the New South Wales attack, moving from eight to 91 in just 41 balls.
Young's first eight runs had taken 78 deliveries.

New South Wales pace bowler Phil Alley ended the South Australia innings when he trapped Harrity leg before wicket for two, leaving Young stranded on 91 not out. Alley, who tore through the South Australia top order late on Sunday, finished with five for 89 from 21 overs.
The win saw New South Wales move into third place in the Shield standings behind unbeaten leaders Queensland and Western Australia. South Australia have yet to record a point after four matches.
In Perth, Western Australia had little trouble in reaching their winning target of 121 after bowling Victoria out for 283 in the second innings.
Western Australia scored 121 for three, with first innings century-maker Mike Hussey steering his side to a seven-wicket victory with a rapid 50.
Earlier, Victoria could add only 62 to their overnight score of 221 for six.
